purpose: Freeze the first three actual-process transport cases for machine-authority serialization and pre-admission worker behavior. The remaining transport obligations and full H2 acceptance remain pending.

scope.acceptance_limit: This is a transport-case authoring subledger only. It grants no execution authorization and makes no H2 acceptance claim.

method: Run only after the complete full-H2 ledger, contract, runner, independent and TC reviews, and pre-gate approval. The transport phase uses the qualified H1 Python environment and explicitly loads tests.ifpmic_api.h2_transport_case_budget. Its protocol hook begins before session fixture setup, measures the case body/setup to 215 seconds and one shared fixture/process cleanup epoch to 25 seconds, and writes a unique private timing record. Each test uses actual isolated PostgreSQL, G5 physical READY, a real owned Temporal server and production CLI/Dispatcher; constructor-injected barriers pause only the named SQL/Dispatcher edge. Private SQL snapshots, exact barrier event times, process PID/start-tick journals and direct Temporal history observations are retained under the runner-provided private evidence root. Shared fixture pins reflect the current authoring checkpoint; the complete inventory and runtime qualification remain pending.
agent: TC owns this test module, test-only child, budget plugin and subledger. Root owns shared fixture closure and full runner/contract integration. No tests, imports, SQL, services or network activity were run for this authoring checkpoint.

timing.justification: All three cases create and stop an actual Temporal CLI server and use the real PostgreSQL session fixtures. The bounded allowance includes those owned process and fixture lifecycles; the shared cleanup interval does not reset per process or fixture.

cases.purpose: A disabled dispatcher principal is rejected before it can claim a fresh accepted create.
cases.target: Actual production Dispatcher startup against the registered deployment after owner disables that principal; the synthetic accepted job is fresh and has no execution binding.
cases.method: Create an accepted job through the real G4/G5 harness, establish physical READY, disable the registered dispatcher principal through the owner role, then start the one-shot production Dispatcher child. Independently compare owner SQL before and after and query the exact workflow ID in the actual isolated Temporal namespace.
cases.pass_criteria: The CLI exits with fixed dependency-unavailable status before claim; the full job/outbox/workspace snapshot is unchanged; bindings, attempts, scopes and receipts remain empty; independent Temporal listing returns no execution.
cases.expected: Startup authorization denies before claim and before any StartWorkflow RPC.
cases.evidence: Private before/after SQL snapshots, fixed child exit/output, process identity lifecycle and independent exact-workflow-ID listing.
cases.recovery: Preserve the failure evidence and stop only owned children/server; do not reactivate the principal or repair the job to make the case pass.

cases.purpose: A principal disable waiting on the claim transaction commits before execution reservation is authorized.
cases.target: Fresh accepted create with no binding, a real Dispatcher child paused before and after the claim transaction, and a separate owner SQL session disabling the dispatcher registration.
cases.method: Pause at the real ExecutionStore before_claim_delivery_commit hook and observe the owner UPDATE blocked via pg_blocking_pids and lock wait state. Release claim commit, pause at after_claim_delivery_commit before Dispatcher proceeds to deliver/reserve, verify the owner disable committed, then release delivery. Independently verify no reservation, attempt completion, scope, receipt or Temporal execution.
cases.pass_criteria: The observed database lock ordering is claim transaction before disable commit, but fresh unbound create has no SQL start authorization: the subsequent real reserve_execution rechecks the disabled principal and returns dependency wait. Outbox remains the same generation-1 leased claim, no execution binding or effect is created, and no exact workflow history exists.
cases.expected: Principal disable is serialized after claim commit and before reserve authorization; claim alone does not authorize StartWorkflow.
cases.evidence: Both literal store-phase barrier events, blocked owner backend PID plus pg_blocking_pids observation, committed disabled-principal row, before/after owner snapshots, dispatcher lifecycle and direct Temporal listing.
cases.recovery: Preserve event ordering and snapshots; release every private barrier and clean only owned processes under the shared deadline. Do not assert cancellation of any already-reserved or in-flight authorized RPC.

cases.purpose: A real projector activity arriving before dispatcher admission waits without effects, then succeeds for the same run after admission.
cases.target: Actual production Dispatcher paused after it observes persisted Started history but before admit_run, plus a separate production Worker CLI on the registered build queue.
cases.method: Pause the actual Dispatcher at after_history_observed after its one real Start and independent history read. Start the real registered Worker; independently observe a completed read_activation activity returning wait while workflow phase remains admission_wait. Snapshot SQL to require DRAFT revision 0, reserved binding with no admitted_run_id, generation-1 leased outbox, and no worker scope or receipt. Release the dispatcher, require admission/ack and project_activation to settle, and assert exactly the same Started run is admitted and the one immutable receipt queues the job.
cases.pass_criteria: Before release, actual worker history proves wait and no project_activation activity is scheduled; SQL business state remains unchanged with no scope or receipt. After release, the same observed run is admitted once, the original command is dispatched, one scope and sequence-1 receipt exist, and the actual workflow remains queued with no replacement Started event.
cases.expected: Pre-admission activity has zero business effects; admission later enables projection for the same run only.
cases.evidence: Raw first-Started history, actual activity completion/history IDs, pre/post owner snapshots and hashes, exact run ID, G5 tree oracle, process PID/start-tick journal and bounded cleanup record.
cases.recovery: Preserve all observations and stop only the owned dispatcher, worker and Temporal server; never synthesize admission, receipt or worker output.
